transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood), Laura Chen (Redwood), Jordan Weiss (Redwood), Maya Rodriguez (Blue Horizon), Ethan Cole (Blue Horizon), Priya Singh (Blue Horizon), Alex Torres (Blue Horizon)

Summary: Quick hosted API demo focused on chat/text generation basics: streaming, parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), retries and best practices for reliability and cost. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for an in-app assistant; primary concerns are latency, cost, and security/compliance.

00:00 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm samir from redwood, i'll kick us off.
00:06 Maya: hi, thanks. excited to see how this could fit into our driver support assistant.
00:10 Samir: quick agenda — demo the hosted api chat endpoint, show streaming, walk through key params, retry behavior, and then q&a.
00:18 Laura: i'll jump in on the technical bits and cover security notes near the end.
00:24 Ethan: perfect. our main thing is around tail latency during peak dispatch times and also cost per convo.
00:30 Samir: got it. and you mentioned compliance — priya, anything top-line we should know?
00:35 Priya: we're SOC2 aligned, need audit logs and kms integration, plus data residency for EU drivers.
00:42 Samir: noted, we support kms, audit logs — i'll share docs.
00:47 Jordan: ok starting the demo — sharing screen, here's a sample POST to /v1/chat: messages array, model param, and stream flag.
00:57 Laura: one thing to call out — streaming returns chunked events as tokens come back, so you can render partial responses quickly.
01:07 Ethan: if we stream, do we still get the full response in a single final event?
01:12 Jordan: yes, stream sends incremental delta events and a final completion event. if you prefer, you can do non-streaming for simpler clients.
01:20 Samir: here's an example node snippet, set stream=true, listen for data frames, assemble finish. also show python requests example. (link shared: https://redwood.ai/quickstart)
01:40 Laura: about params — temperature controls randomness, top_p for nucleus sampling; lower temps for deterministic replies for policy content, higher for creative drafting. max_tokens caps length to avoid runaway.
01:55 Maya: what's our typical default?
01:58 Jordan: default we demo is temp=0.2, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=256 for assistant replies. you can tune per-route.
02:10 Ethan: curious about safety filters and moderation API — do you run models through a classifier pre- or post-response?
02:16 Laura: we have optional post-generation moderation hooks and you can route flagged items to a safe-mode model.
02:25 Priya: encryption in transit and at rest? where do keys live?
02:29 Samir: TLS in transit, at-rest with customer-managed KMS in dedicated/private; for hosted we also support KMS integration and provide key rotation logs.
02:38 Ethan: latency — what's realistic p50/p95 for short prompts (20 tokens) on hosted?
02:44 Jordan: depends on model; for our curated small-medium models you can expect p50 ~ 60-120ms and p95 ~ 300-450ms for single-turn short prompts, larger models higher. we can share our perf profiles.
02:58 Maya: that's promising. what about concurrency and rate limits?
03:02 Samir: hosted has per-account rate limits, plus burst windows; we can discuss quota increases if you commit to dedicated. retries on 429/5xx handled client-side with exponential backoff — recommended pattern is jittered backoff and idempotency keys for non-chat tasks.
03:20 Jordan: show retry example: on 429 wait 500ms, then 1s, then 2s — but for streaming connections we recommend reconnect instead of aggressive retries to avoid duplicate tokens.
03:33 Ethan: how do you protect against duplicate processing if we reconnect?
03:36 Laura: use request_id in metadata, server responds with duplicate suppression when detected for short windows.
03:44 Jordan: demo continuing — now toggling streaming off to show final response body with usage fields: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_cost_estimate.
03:58 Maya: can we get token-level cost breakdowns?
04:01 Samir: yep, console shows token cost per model and per-call. plus per-route rollups in operations.
04:10 Alex: any SDKs? our stack is node + golang.
04:14 Jordan: official SDKs for node/python, golang community SDKs we support; examples here -> link (https://redwood.ai/sdk).
04:23 Ethan: about batching — can hosted batch multiple user messages to save cost?
04:28 Jordan: yes, our runtime does continuous batching where possible. for chat you can batch independent requests; for single-session flows batching is trickier due to context. our Optimize product suggests batching settings per workload.
04:41 Priya: for EU residency, does hosted store data in region?
04:45 Samir: hosted has region control; you can pin to eu-west region and we honor data residency. for strict controls we recommend Private.
04:53 Maya: can you do canary rollouts of model versions?
04:56 Laura: yes — per-route model pinning and rollout policies with canary % and automatic fallback on regressions.
05:06 Ethan: demo question — how do we measure regressions?
05:09 Jordan: integrate eval sets and perf/quality alerts; Redwood Optimize watches prompt tests and raises alerts on BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics or custom rules.
05:20 Alex: reliability during peak — if the hosted region is saturated what happens?
05:24 Samir: smart routing falls back to compatible model variants or other regions based on policy; for strict SLOs Dedicated gives capacity guarantees.
05:33 Maya: ok let's talk pricing — ballpark cost per 1k short-conversations?
05:37 Samir: i'll send the detailed sheet but rough hosted avg depends on model and tokens; for our curated medium model ~ $2-6 per 1k short convos (varies).
05:48 Ethan: for our POC we need a simple retry and streaming test harness — we can provide sample payloads.
05:52 Samir: great, jordan will run a benchmark too.
05:56 Jordan: noted — i'll capture a streaming+retry run and share logs and p50/p95 numbers.
06:02 Priya: final security Q — can we get a time-limited access token and audit logs for dev teams?
06:07 Laura: yes, tokens with scopes and expiry + full audit logs in console. for enterprise we tie to SSO/SAML and RBAC.
06:15 Maya: ok next steps sound good. thanks everyone.
06:18 Samir: recap: we'll send pricing, security docs, run benchmark and schedule poc scoping.
06:22 Ethan: thanks, talk soon.
